newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: S.Africa forex reforms to boost Zambia bourse.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa forex reforms to boost Zambia bourse.

text.p: The relaxation of South Africa's exchange controls are likely to boost the growth of the Lusaka Stock Exchange, which has been the best performing stock market on the continent this year, exchange officials said on Monday.
The South African government partially relaxed foreign exchange controls on July 1 to allow South Africans to invest some of their funds offshore.

"Of particular interest to the Lusaka Stock Exchange is the provision in these new rules that specifically promote investment in listed companies in Southern African Development Community (SADC) countries," exchange general manager Charles Mate said.

"The move significantly opens the boundaries, making it possible for companies listed on the Lusaka stock exchange to raise capital both domestically as well as regionally from South African-based investors.
"Specifically, this should be of particular importance to those companies operating in Zambia that have strong links with South Africa," he added.

The Lusaka Stock Exchange was poised to grow over the next few months, with the development of new investment vehicles such as unit trusts, the quotation of Mufulira Wanderers Football Club, and further interactions with foreign investors.
Mate said the Lusaka bourse had been the fastest growing in Africa as at mid-year.
"On July 31, the Lusaka Stock Exchange index closed at 242.36, up 142 percent since January 1. This corresponds to a rise of 140 percent in dollar terms," Mate said.
"At the same time, the market capitalisation has risen $216 million in January to $502 million at the end of July," he added.
Mate said the main concern of many investors was whether these gains were sustainable, and whether there was an adequate supply of stock on the market, adding that their fears were unjustified.

"The exchange does not yet suffer the problem of large stocks of shares tied up with institutions or a few individuals. The free float is still quite large - for example, Rothmans has 50 percent of its issued shares in public hands. The stock, however, is still trading on a PE as low as 4.27," he said.
He said economic indicators, which showed inflation down at 22 percent in July, a stable exchange rate and declining interest rates, should give confidence to the market.

"There is also increasing interest by private sector companies, particularly banks, to list on the exchange and take advantage of the tax incentives as well as the opportunity to raise capital on the back of the strong demand for shares in the market," Mate said.
